subject: Private Endpoint Outbound Controls: Minimal-Trust Egress Plan
messages:
From: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>
Cc: acme-security@acme.com
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy egress — minimal outbound surface we need from Redwood PE

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we scope the on-prem private endpoint (PE) deployment, our security team needs a concise, prescriptive outbound allowlist and firewall policy that we can present to our network ops and compliance reviewers. Key asks: 

- A single canonical list of IP ranges (or domain patterns where necessary) used by Redwood control plane, telemetry, metrics, KMS, and optional marketplace fetches.
- Ports/protocols per flow and whether TLS termination or mutual TLS is used.
- Guidance on DNS resolution (use of FQDN allowlist vs IPs) and handling of rotated IPs.
- Requirement for a forward proxy, egress NAT, or both; recommended placement (gateway vs host).
- How to validate connectivity without exposing sensitive keys or data to Redwood hosted infra.
- A short runbook for onboarding the first dev cluster behind our firewall.

We have an upcoming internal review on Friday afternoon — can you share the allowlist + a short onboarding runbook? I've attached our high-level network diagram for context.

Regards,
Rajiv
Sr. InfoSec Engineer, Acme Corp

Attachments referenced: acme-network-overview.pdf (attached in our system)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example>
To: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@acme.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, hannah_schmitt@redwood.example
Date: 2027-04-06T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy egress — minimal outbound surface we need from Redwood PE

Rajiv / team —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below is a pragmatic, minimal-trust egress plan tailored for a private endpoint (VPC/on-prem) deployment that both minimizes outbound surface and keeps your data plane fully inside your network. This is formatted so network ops can paste rules into firewalls or proxy configs. I'll attach the CSV of IP ranges and a draft runbook.

Executive summary (short):
- Allow only outbound traffic from the PE control plane hosts to the following destination categories: Redwood control-plane management, artifact fetch (model blobs), telemetry ingestion (opt-in), KMS endpoints (if using Redwood KMS integration), and optionally cloud storage endpoints (S3-compatible) for snapshot uploads. All other outbound flows should be deny-by-default.
- Prefer domain-based allowlist for service endpoints when using a corporate forward proxy with SNI inspection; otherwise use the fixed IP ranges listed in the attached CSV. We support both modes.

Canonical destination list (recommended):
1) Control plane API endpoints (management and auth):
   - Dest FQDNs: api.redwood-inference.com, auth.redwood-inference.com
   - Ports: 443 (HTTPS)
   - IPs: see attachments (we publish a small set of static /24s per region). If you require IPs only, use the CSV.

2) Artifact & model blob downloads:
   - Dest FQDNs: artifacts.redwood-inference.com or s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com (depending on model source)
   - Ports: 443
   - Note: model blobs can be large; recommend allowing destination CIDRs for artifact hosts and rate-limiting per host.

3) Telemetry (optional / customer-configurable):
   - Dest FQDN: telemetry.redwood-inference.com
   - Ports: 443
   - If telemetry is disallowed, we will disable outbound telemetry and provide a local log delivery option (file drop or push to your syslog/collector).

4) KMS / Key management endpoints (if using Redwood-managed KMS integration):
   - Dest: kms.redwood-inference.com or customer-specific KMS endpoints (e.g., aws-kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com)
   - Ports: 443
   - If you require KMS traffic to stay within your VPC/VPN to your own KMS, we support bringing-your-own-KMS and will default to customer-owned endpoints.

5) Marketplace or plugin registries (optional):
   - Dest: marketplace.redwood-inference.com (443).

Network/NAT/Proxy guidance:
- Egress NAT: Place a small NAT gateway cluster in the DMZ that maps PE outbound to a predictable set of public IPs. We publish the list of Redwood ingress IPs that need to be whitelisted on your edge for call-backs, but for outbound allowlisting you should prefer destination IPs/domains rather than source IPs.
- Forward Proxy: If your environment requires domain-level allowlisting or TLS inspection, put a forward proxy with SNI-aware rules in front of the NAT. We recommend configuring the proxy to allow CONNECT to the specific FQDNs above. If TLS interception is performed, mutual TLS validation must be disabled for Redwood client TLS to the control plane (we rely on cert validation).
- mTLS: Redwood supports mutual TLS for control-plane webhook callbacks only if you register a client cert; otherwise all control-plane API traffic uses standard TLS with certificate pinning.
- DNS: Prefer split-horizon DNS so FQDNs resolve to internal addresses when inside the VPC. If you cannot use DNS, allow the IP ranges in the CSV. If you use domain allowlisting, ensure your proxy respects SNI for CONNECT flows to avoid DNS-over-HTTPS pitfalls.

Firewall rules (paste-friendly examples):
- Deny all outbound by default from PE subnets to 0.0.0.0/0 except:
  - ALLOW tcp 443 -> api.redwood-inference.com (or IP CIDRs in egress-ips.csv)
  - ALLOW tcp 443 -> artifacts.redwood-inference.com (or artifact CIDR)
  - ALLOW tcp 443 -> telemetry.redwood-inference.com (if opt-in)
  - ALLOW tcp 443 -> kms.redwood-inference.com (only if using Redwood-managed KMS)

- Example iptables (host-level minimal nat):
  iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 203.0.113.0/24 --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
  iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP

Operational recommendations: 
- IP rotation & Notice: We publish a weekly change log. If you use FQDNs + proxy, rotations are transparent. If you require static IPs, subscribe to our IP-change webhook and schedule change windows.
- Health & validation: Run an internal smoke test that performs TLS handshake + API login + model blob fetch. We can provide a lightweight test client that performs those checks without sending production data.
- Monitoring: Alert on RST/timeout to the control-plane IPs and failed TLS handshakes. Provide us the anonymized connectivity traces if a debugging session is needed.
- Fallbacks: Configure a canary route that allows outbound to a cached model store (local mirror) if control-plane calls fail; this avoids breakage for inference-only flows.

Security notes:
- We never send customer prompt content to third-party telemetry unless explicitly enabled and consented.
- If your environment performs TLS inspection, do not use mutual-TLS client certificates with Redwood control plane (it breaks cert validation).

Attached items: egress-ips.csv (canonical CIDRs per region), private-endpoint-runbook-v1.docx (onboarding steps), network-diagram-az1.png

Onboarding runbook (brief):
1) Provision PE hosts in your VPC/subnet and ensure route to NAT/proxy.
2) Apply deny-all egress baseline on PE subnets.
3) Apply the allow rules above (use domain or IP mode as chosen).
4) Run the smoke test client and capture logs.
5) Authorize access window and monitor for 24 hours.

If you'd like, Marissa and I can run a 30-minute technical onboarding with your network ops team and I can join to walk through the firewall/NAT/proxy text.

—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Dev / Evelyn —

This looks great and exactly what our reviewers asked for. A couple of follow-ups before we close our change ticket: 

1) We prefer IP-only allowlisting for the initial rollout — please confirm the CSV contains the full set per region and your change-notice cadence.
2) Can you provide the smoke-test client you mentioned as a single binary/script and a short checklist for the SOC reviewer so they can validate without handing over keys?
3) We plan to place a forward proxy with CONNECT-only rules (no TLS interception). Confirm that will work with Redwood clients if the proxy allows SNI passthrough.

If you can confirm the above and drop the CSV and runbook into the SharePoint link I sent earlier, we'll schedule the firewall change for next Wednesday. Marissa — can we set a 30-min handoff with Network Ops for Thursday morning?

Thanks —
Rajiv
